name: Ayodhya, 1992
summary: Kar sevaks brought down the Babri Masjid in Ayodhya on 6 December 1992. That night the town’s remaining Muslim lanes were burned; in the weeks that followed, riots ran through Uttar Pradesh and much of the country. Bombay is a separate campaign. The Liberhan Commission later called the demolition planned, not a spasm.
scaleRationale: A national political rupture. The mosque’s fall redrew party politics; the riot wave killed about two to three thousand people across India.

resources.note: Ramjanmabhoomi claim on the mosque site

end.note: UP wave peaked in December; Bombay’s second wave is recorded under bombay-1992.

name: Meerut, 1987
summary: Communal clashes in Meerut in May 1987, after the Babri locks were opened the year before, turned into two police days that still structure the city’s memory. PAC men trucked Muslim youths from Hashimpura to a canal and shot them. The next afternoon they walked into Maliana. Hashimpura produced a life sentence thirty-one years later. Maliana produced an acquittal.
scaleRationale: A district killing wave: official tallies in the low hundreds, Hashimpura and Maliana alone around a hundred Muslim dead, and a legal afterlife measured in decades.

start.note: Street clashes from mid-May; Hashimpura 22 May, Maliana 23 May.

name: Moradabad, 1980
summary: Eid al-Fitr, 13 August 1980. A pig at the city Eidgah, a crush of namazis, and police fire into the crowd. Two constables died when a chowki was burned. What followed for weeks was a police–Muslim confrontation that became a Hindu–Muslim riot and spread into neighbouring districts. The Saxena Commission sat; the numbers never settled.
scaleRationale: A city-and-district killing wave lasting weeks. Official counts sit in the dozens to low hundreds; contemporaneous reporting went higher.

end.note: Violence continued into neighbouring districts into early 1981.

parties.note: PAC reinforced local police after the Eidgah firing.

sources.title: The Moradabad riots of 1980: The incident and its political fallout

sources.note: Saxena Commission: 83 dead in communal rioting. Then home minister Swarup Kumari Bakshi told the Assembly the statewide dead-and-missing figure was 289.

killed.note: Government records cited by Indian Express put Moradabad itself at 83 dead and 112 injured. Contemporaneous press often said 300–400. Scholarly visitors that winter (Saberwal and Hasan) heard community counts much higher; those remain unverified here.

historiography.claim: A pig, a stampede, and a leadership tussle among Muslim politicians explain the dead.

name: Bhagalpur, 1989
summary: A Ramshila procession and a bomb in Bhagalpur town on 24 October 1989 opened two months of killing across the district. Inquiry judges later wrote that rumours, police, and the press moved together. Whole Muslim weaver villages were emptied. At Logain the dead were buried under a cauliflower field.
scaleRationale: Around a thousand dead, some 250 villages, fifty thousand displaced — a district pogrom with a national afterlife.

resources.note: Inquiry and later trials described land grabs after Muslim families fled.

name: Muzaffarnagar, 2013
summary: Three deaths at Kawal on 27 August 2013, a mahapanchayat, a circulated video, and then two days in which Jat and Muslim villages in Muzaffarnagar and Shamli burned each other. Tens of thousands left and many did not go home. The state later told the Supreme Court that 46 of the dead were Muslim and 16 Hindu.
scaleRationale: A multi-district riot with a documented death toll in the sixties and displacement in the tens of thousands — the worst Hindu–Muslim killing in Uttar Pradesh in a decade.

name: Ranvir Sena / central Bihar caste war
summary: A Bhumihar landlord militia, founded in Bhojpur in 1994 to fight CPI-ML and MCC squads, spent the late 1990s killing Dalit and Muslim labourers in their hamlets — women and children first, the Sena said, so that Naxalites would not grow up. Bathani Tola and Laxmanpur Bathe are the two days that still have names. The other side of that caste war, the MCC and Liberation massacres of upper-caste villagers, sits on the Naxal campaign.
scaleRationale: A multi-district militia campaign over several years. HRW put Ranvir Sena killings of Dalits above 400 between 1995 and 1999; the two emblematic massacres alone killed about eighty people.

end.note: Commander Brahmeshwar Singh arrested 2002; the large massacres cluster 1996–2000. He was shot in Arrah in 2012.
